"Swedish is a V2 language: the finite verb is the second constituent of a main clause, so fronting anything at all pushes the subject behind the verb. Write *I morgon åker vi till Malmö*, never *I morgon vi åker till Malmö*. This is the single most common structural tell of a text drafted in English and rendered into Swedish.

Where a compound grows unreadably long, rewrite it into a prepositional phrase rather than splitting it.

Definiteness is marked twice. An adjective before a definite noun takes both the front article and the noun's suffix: *den nya rapporten*, *det stora huset*, *de svenska kunderna*. English has one article and drafts translated from it routinely lose one of the two Swedish markers.

*Du* is the default address in Swedish prose, including business and journalism. *Ni* to a single reader is either archaic or a deliberate distancing, and reads as a translation from a language that has a formal pronoun.

*Man* is a fallback rather than the ordinary generic pronoun. It is justified where the agent genuinely is anybody at all or is genuinely unknown, and where naming one would claim more than the material carries. Where the sentence has a real subject to hand — the reader, the writer, the organisation, the profession, the study — that subject is what the sentence takes. Genitive takes a bare *s* with no apostrophe: *Kntnts kunder*, *Sveriges riksdag*. A name already ending in *s*, *x*, or *z* takes nothing at all: *Anders bok*, *Marx teori*.

Swedish tolerates a shorter sentence than English does and punishes subordination harder. Prefer a main clause with a fronted adverbial to a long relative construction, and prefer a verb to a nominalisation: *när kommunen beslutade* over *vid kommunens beslutsfattande*.

Reach for the established Swedish term where one exists and the field actually uses it — *återkoppling*, *underlag*, *avstämning* — but do not purge the loanwords a professional reader expects. A text that writes *dator* and *webbplats* naturally is Swedish; a text that hunts down every English term and replaces it with a coinage nobody says is not."

1	# Case-study brief and source
2	
3	SYNTHETIC EVALUATION MATERIAL. This is the entire fictional source package. Source language: English. No external facts or quotations may be added.
4	
5	## Brief
6	
7	Write a journalistic customer case for operations managers at small housing companies. The publisher is the supplier, Svale Systems. The customer, Elm Quay Housing, should remain the acting party. Approximately 400 words, as material allows. Markdown. No author name supplied. The optional next step is the supplied implementation checklist at https://example.invalid/svale/checklist; it is a document to read, not a consultation booking or a product trial.
8	
9	## Material
10	
11	Elm Quay Housing manages 640 flats. In September 2025 its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings. Previously telephone reports and emails were stored separately. The team wanted staff on different shifts to see the same information. It chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair. No comparison with another supplier is available.
12	
13	The maintenance team designed its categories and kept telephone reporting open for residents. Svale configured the log and trained six staff during two sessions. The trial lasted eight weeks. Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered. It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial. Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period. The periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software. There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements.
14	
15	Customer interview with maintenance supervisor Maya Lind, complete usable quotations:
16	
17	- “We wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done. The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log.”
18	- “We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports. I would set that time aside before the next building starts.”
19	- “I would choose to do the trial again. Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation.”
20	
21	Lind did not recommend Svale to every housing company. Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment. It is not an inference from the figures. The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs. The supplier approved publication of this case as supplier-published material; it is not independent journalism. All interviews occurred by email, and no physical scene, emotion or remembered dialogue is provided. Translation of the quotations is permitted, preserving stance and qualification.
22	
23	## Forbidden inferences / judging
24	
25	No claim that software caused the shorter assignment time, saved money, delighted residents or rescued a helpless customer. Do not turn assignment time into completion time. The customer's reservation must survive. Judge whether quotations contribute experience beyond the surrounding narrative, whether supplier narration stays in third person and whether the suggested link accurately describes its destination.

1	# Elm Quay fick en samlad bild av felanmälningarna
2	
3	I två av sina hus provade Elm Quay Housings underhållsteam en gemensam reparationslogg från Svale Systems i åtta veckor. Teamet byggde själv upp kategorierna. För den som planerar något liknande visar erfarenheterna var förberedelserna tar tid, vad testets siffror säger och inte säger och hur arbetsledaren Maya Lind bedömer resultatet.
4	
5	Av Thomas Barregren
6	
7	Hos Elm Quay Housing, som förvaltar 640 lägenheter, sparades felanmälningar per telefon och mejl tidigare var för sig. I september 2025 beslutade bolagets eget underhållsteam att pröva en gemensam reparationslogg i två hus. Leverantören blev Svale Systems. Efter åtta veckors test har teamet siffror med tydliga förbehåll och en bild av vad arbetsledaren skulle göra annorlunda.
8	
9	## Varför teamet ville ha en gemensam logg
10	
11	Maya Lind är arbetsledare i underhållsteamet. I en mejlintervju beskriver hon vad teamet var ute efter:
12	
13	– Vi ville att kvällsskiftet skulle se vad morgonskiftet redan hade gjort. Kategorierna var våra egna; Svale hjälpte oss att föra in dem i loggen.
14	
15	Innan teamet bestämde sig för Svale testade det om loggen kunde visa status för varje reparation. Uppgifter om någon jämförelse med andra leverantörer finns inte.
16	
17	## Teamet och Svale delade på införandet
18	
19	Underhållsteamet lät de boende fortsätta att felanmäla per telefon. Svale konfigurerade loggen och utbildade sex anställda vid två tillfällen. Testet pågick i åtta veckor.
20	
21	Lind har ett råd om tidsplanen:
22	
23	– Vi lade mer tid på att komma överens om kategorierna än på att föra in de första anmälningarna. Den tiden skulle jag avsätta innan det är dags för nästa hus.
24

26

28

Perioderna hade olika arbetsbelastning, och anteckningen tillskriver uttryckligen inte programvaran skillnaden. Mätningar av kostnader, de boendes nöjdhet och tid till avslutad reparation saknas.
30	
31	## Maya Lind ser tillbaka på testet
32	
33	Lind rekommenderade inte Svale till alla bostadsbolag. Om testet i de egna husen skriver hon:
34	
35	– Jag skulle välja att göra testet igen. Att ha en enda vy över anmälningarna hjälper oss, men jag skulle planera in en extra vecka för förberedelserna.
36	
37	## Kategorierna ska prövas på större reparationer

1	# Quoting speech
2	
3	Read this before putting quotation marks around anything somebody said. It applies to interview transcripts, recorded remarks, meeting notes, and any other material where the words are a person's rather than a document's.
4	
5	Speech is not written prose, and a transcript quoted raw reads as carelessness towards the speaker rather than fidelity to them. So a spoken quotation may be repaired — cautiously, within a boundary that is easier to state than to feel your way to.
6	
7	When translating permitted quotations, preserve meaning, stance, certainty and distinctive voice in idiomatic target-language speech, not source-language syntax. The restrictions below protect that substance; they do not require word-for-word translation. Make an implicit referent explicit only when the supplied context settles it. Where the meaning remains ambiguous, paraphrase what is established rather than inventing a fluent interpretation.
8	
9	## What may be repaired
10	
11	The syntax of speech: a sentence abandoned halfway and restarted, a subject left behind by its verb, a clause that never closes. Fillers — *you know*, *sort of*, *liksom*, *alltså* — where they carry nothing. Repetition that is the speaker searching for a word rather than insisting on one. False starts, and the small disfluencies a person does not hear themselves make.
12	
13	That is the whole list. Everything on it is noise the speaker did not intend to produce, and removing it leaves what they meant to say.
14	
15	## What may not
16	
17	**Meaning.** Not narrowed, not widened, not sharpened. A speaker who said *most of them* has not said *all of them*, and one who said *we looked at it* has not said *we rejected it*.
18	
19	**Stance.** Approval stays approval, reluctance stays reluctance, and a speaker who was careful not to blame anybody is not made to blame somebody by a tidier sentence.
20	
21	**Certainty.** *I think*, *probably*, *as far as I know*, and *we are not sure yet* are the claim, not padding on it. Removing a hedge manufactures a confidence the speaker did not have; adding one takes away a confidence they did.
22	
23	**Distinctive wording.** Where the speaker reached for an unusual word, an image, a piece of slang, or a phrasing that is theirs, it stays. Smoothing it into the register of the surrounding article is the most tempting of these failures and the one a reader can least detect.
24	
25	**A self-correction.** Where a speaker gives a number or a fact and then corrects it, the correction is what they said. Quoting the first version is a misquotation; quoting a version that never existed — the correction with the correcting away — is worse.
26	
27	**Anything additive.** Add no new meaning: no fact, stance, certainty, name, figure or connection that the speaker did not supply. A permitted repair or translation may change words only to render that same meaning.
28	
29	## When to paraphrase instead
30	
31	Where fidelity is uncertain, paraphrase. A paraphrase that attributes carefully — *she said the change had taken about a year, and that she was not sure it would hold* — is accurate, useful, and honest about what the material supports. A fluent direct quotation assembled out of a fragmentary answer is none of those things, however good it sounds.
32	
33	The cases that should turn into paraphrase: material that is a summary of what somebody said rather than their words; a transcript too broken to repair inside the boundary above; several remarks that would have to be welded together to make one sentence; and any moment where you find yourself choosing between two readings of what the speaker meant.
34	
35	Signal what the material actually is. Where the source is notes rather than a recording, the text says what the person said and does not pretend to their exact wording.
36	
37	## What stays outside this
38	
39	Whether the speaker approves the quotation. Quote approval is a human arrangement between the writer and the person quoted, and nothing here verifies it or stands in for it. A draft may say a quotation is unapproved; it may not treat the absence of approval as a problem it has solved.
40

# Claim accounting: draft against source

Draft: `scratch/write-run.JVVig0/draft.md` (Swedish). Material: `work/source.md` (English). Quotations are translated from English. The byline "Av Thomas Barregren" comes from the invocation and is not assessed.

## 1. Claim-by-claim accounting

Each entry gives the draft passage, the source passage it rests on (verbatim, in English), and what differs.

**C1. Title:** "Elm Quay fick en samlad bild av felanmälningarna"
- Source: "decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings"; Lind: "Having one view of the reports helps us"; "kept telephone reporting open for residents"; "The trial has not yet expanded".
- Difference: the subject is the whole company ("Elm Quay"), and the object is definite and unrestricted ("felanmälningarna", meaning the fault reports in general). The source limits the shared log to a trial in two buildings run by the maintenance team, and the "one view" is Lind's assessment ("helps us"). The source does not say whether phone reports were entered into the log. **Finding F1.**

**C2. Lead:** "I två av sina hus provade Elm Quay Housings underhållsteam en gemensam reparationslogg från Svale Systems i åtta veckor."
- Source: "its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings"; "The trial lasted eight weeks."; "It chose Svale Systems".
- Difference: none material. "sina hus" (reflexive, pointing to the team) means buildings under the team's care, not ownership.

**C3. Lead:** "Teamet byggde själv upp kategorierna."
- Source: "The maintenance team designed its categories"; Lind: "The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log."; "Svale configured the log".
- Difference: "designed" became "byggde själv upp" ("built up by itself"). *Bygga upp* also covers setting the categories up in the system, and *själv* excludes help. **Finding F2** (minor).

**C4. Lead:** "…visar erfarenheterna var förberedelserna tar tid, vad testets siffror säger och inte säger och hur arbetsledaren Maya Lind bedömer resultatet."
- Source: Lind: "We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports."; the trial note and its exclusions; "Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment."
- Difference: none. This is the author's framing of supported material.

**C5. Para 1:** "Hos Elm Quay Housing, som förvaltar 640 lägenheter, …"
- Source: "Elm Quay Housing manages 640 flats."
- Difference: none.

**C6. Para 1:** "…sparades felanmälningar per telefon och mejl tidigare var för sig."
- Source: "Previously telephone reports and emails were stored separately."
- Difference: the source names "telephone reports" and "emails", and does not say the emails were fault reports. The draft turns both into fault reports ("felanmälningar per telefon och mejl"). **Finding F3.** The term "felanmälan" is also covered under F4.

**C7. Para 1:** "I september 2025 beslutade bolagets eget underhållsteam att pröva en gemensam reparationslogg i två hus."
- Source: "In September 2025 its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings."
- Difference: none.

**C8. Para 1:** "Leverantören blev Svale Systems."
- Source: "It chose Svale Systems after testing…"
- Difference: the agent is not stated in this sentence, but C11 restores it ("Innan teamet bestämde sig för Svale"). No support problem.

**C9. Para 1:** "Efter åtta veckors test har teamet siffror med tydliga förbehåll och en bild av vad arbetsledaren skulle göra annorlunda."
- Source: "The trial lasted eight weeks."; "the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software"; "It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial."; Lind: "I would set that time aside before the next building starts"; "I would leave an extra week for preparation".
- Difference: none material. "tydliga" rests on "explicitly", and "annorlunda" rests on Lind's "extra week" and "set that time aside".

**C10. H2 and para:** "Varför teamet ville ha en gemensam logg" / "Maya Lind är arbetsledare i underhållsteamet. I en mejlintervju beskriver hon vad teamet var ute efter"
- Source: "The team wanted staff on different shifts to see the same information."; "maintenance supervisor Maya Lind"; "All interviews occurred by email"; Lind: "The categories were ours" (she speaks as a team member).
- Difference: none. "arbetsledare" is a fair rendering of "maintenance supervisor", and her membership of the team is carried by her "we/ours".

**C11.** "Innan teamet bestämde sig för Svale testade det om loggen kunde visa status för varje reparation."
- Source: "It chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair."
- Difference: none. The draft, like the source, leaves the test result unstated.

**C12.** "Uppgifter om någon jämförelse med andra leverantörer finns inte."
- Source: "No comparison with another supplier is available."
- Difference: none. The draft keeps the source's state of knowledge (no information, as opposed to "no comparison was made").

**C13. H2:** "Teamet och Svale delade på införandet"
- Source: "The maintenance team designed its categories and kept telephone reporting open for residents. Svale configured the log and trained six staff during two sessions."
- Difference: none material. The heading describes the division of labour the source gives.

**C14.** "Underhållsteamet lät de boende fortsätta att felanmäla per telefon."
- Source: "kept telephone reporting open for residents."
- Difference: none. Reports from residents are what "felanmäla" means.

**C15.** "Svale konfigurerade loggen och utbildade sex anställda vid två tillfällen."
- Source: "Svale configured the log and trained six staff during two sessions."
- Difference: "staff" became "anställda" (employees). **Finding F5** (minor).

**C16.** "Testet pågick i åtta veckor."
- Source: "The trial lasted eight weeks."
- Difference: none.

**C17.** "Lind har ett råd om tidsplanen:"
- Source: Lind: "…I would set that time aside before the next building starts."
- Difference: the draft calls her statement a "råd" (piece of advice). "I would…" is the ordinary form of advice, and the statement is about time planning. Set aside as defensible.

**C18. H2 and paras:** "Elm Quays interna anteckning om testet, daterad den 4 december 2025, anger att 31 felanmälningar fördes in."
- Source: "Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered."
- Difference: the date is attached to the note in the source as well. "repair reports" became "felanmälningar". **Finding F4** (minor).

**C19.** "Anteckningen omfattar inte akuta ärenden eller arbeten som beställdes före testet."
- Source: "It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial."
- Difference: none. In the source, "It" refers to the note, and the draft keeps the note as the subject.

**C20.** "Mediantiden från anmälan till tilldelning var två arbetsdagar under testet och tre under de åtta veckorna dessförinnan."
- Source: "Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period."
- Difference: none. The measure is still assignment time, not completion time.

**C21.** "Perioderna hade olika arbetsbelastning, och anteckningen tillskriver uttryckligen inte programvaran skillnaden."
- Source: "The periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software."
- Difference: none. No causal claim appears anywhere in the draft.

**C22.** "Mätningar av kostnader, de boendes nöjdhet och tid till avslutad reparation saknas."
- Source: "There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements."
- Difference: none.

**C23. H2 and para:** "Maya Lind ser tillbaka på testet" / "Lind rekommenderade inte Svale till alla bostadsbolag."
- Source: "Lind did not recommend Svale to every housing company."
- Difference: none. "inte … alla" keeps the not-all scope of the English.

**C24.** "Om testet i de egna husen skriver hon:"
- Source: "All interviews occurred by email"; Lind: "I would choose to do the trial again."
- Difference: none. "skriver" matches an email interview.

**C25. H2:** "Kategorierna ska prövas på större reparationer"
- Source: "the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs."
- Difference: none material.

**C26.** "Testet har ännu inte utvidgats. Teamet bestämmer sig när det har sett hur kategorierna fungerar för större reparationer."
- Source: "The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs."
- Difference: none.

**C27.** "Den som förbereder ett liknande test kan läsa en [checklista för införandet](…)"
- Source (brief): "The optional next step is the supplied implementation checklist …; it is a document to read, not a consultation booking or a product trial."
- Difference: none. The link is described as something to read, and the draft makes no claim about what the checklist contains. The indefinite "en" does not suggest it is Elm Quay's own checklist.

## 2. Pronouns: person, number and natural gender

| Pronoun (draft) | Referent | Person/number | Natural gender | Support |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| "hon" (C10, C24) | Maya Lind | 3sg | female (natural) | Source: "**Her** final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment." Supported. |
| "det" (C11, C26: "testade det", "när det har sett") | teamet | 3sg | none; neuter is grammatical gender only | Source: "**It** chose…". Supported. |
| "sina" (C2) | underhållsteamet (reflexive) | 3sg possessive | none | Source: "its own maintenance team … two buildings". Supported. |
| "vi", "oss", "våra" (quotations) | the maintenance team including Lind | 1pl | none | Source: "We", "us", "ours". Supported. |
| "jag" (quotations) | Lind | 1sg | none | Source: "I". Supported. |
| "dem" (quotation 1) | kategorierna | 3pl | none | Source: "them". Supported. |
| "Den som" (C27) | generic reader | 3sg generic | none | Author's address. No factual content. |

No pronoun asserts a person, number or natural gender that the source does not carry.

## 3. Translated quotations

- **Q1:** "Vi ville att kvällsskiftet skulle se vad morgonskiftet redan hade gjort. Kategorierna var våra egna; Svale hjälpte oss att föra in dem i loggen."
  - Source: "We wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done. The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log."
  - The meaning, the stance (the categories belong to the customer, Svale helped) and the plain voice are all kept. "våra egna" makes "ours" slightly more emphatic, which matches its contrastive role. Idiomatic, and nothing obstructs the reading.
- **Q2:** "Vi lade mer tid på att komma överens om kategorierna än på att föra in de första anmälningarna. Den tiden skulle jag avsätta innan det är dags för nästa hus."
  - Source: "We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports. I would set that time aside before the next building starts."
  - The comparison and the conditional "would" → "skulle" are both kept. "Den tiden" clearly points back to the time spent agreeing on categories. "innan det är dags för nästa hus" is idiomatic and adds nothing. No obstruction.
- **Q3:** "Jag skulle välja att göra testet igen. Att ha en enda vy över anmälningarna hjälper oss, men jag skulle planera in en extra vecka för förberedelserna."
  - Source: "I would choose to do the trial again. Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation."
  - The qualified stance (would repeat, "helps us", "but" extra week) is kept intact. "leave an extra week" → "planera in en extra vecka" has the same meaning. "en enda vy" reads naturally in a software context. No obstruction.

The brief's own test, whether the quotations add experience beyond the narrative, is met. Q1 gives the shift motive in her words, Q2 gives where the time went, and Q3 gives her qualified verdict. The narrative does not duplicate them.

**No translation findings.**

## 4. Findings

### Source-support findings

**F1. Title widens scope and turns an assessment into a company-level fact** (moderate, CONFIRMED)
- Draft: "Elm Quay fick en samlad bild av felanmälningarna"
- Source: "decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings"; "The trial has not yet expanded"; Lind: "Having one view of the reports helps us".
- Case: Elm Quay manages 640 flats. Fault reports for buildings outside the two-building trial are still handled as before, so Elm Quay as a company does not have a unified view of its fault reports, even though the maintenance team has one for the trial buildings. Nothing in the material excludes this; "The trial has not yet expanded" supports it.
- Smallest repair: restrict the subject and the scope, for example "Elm Quays underhållsteam fick en samlad vy över anmälningarna i två hus". This rests on "shared repair log in two buildings" and "Having one view of the reports helps us".

**F2. "byggde själv upp kategorierna" excludes Svale's part in setting them up** (minor, PLAUSIBLE)
- Draft: "Teamet byggde själv upp kategorierna."
- Source: "The maintenance team designed its categories"; "Svale helped us put them into the log"; "Svale configured the log".
- Case: the team designed the categories, and Svale built them into the log. Then "the team built up the categories by itself" fails for building them in the system, while "designed its categories" holds. The case is taken directly from the material.
- Smallest repair: "Teamet utformade själv kategorierna." Here "själv" is supported by "The categories were ours".

**F3. "emails" narrowed to email fault reports** (moderate, CONFIRMED)
- Draft: "sparades felanmälningar per telefon och mejl tidigare var för sig"
- Source: "Previously telephone reports and emails were stored separately."
- Case: the emails stored separately included correspondence that was not a fault report, such as contractor messages or internal staff emails about repairs. The source statement holds, and the draft's claim that what was stored separately were fault reports by phone and email fails. Nothing in the material says what the emails contained.
- Smallest repair: "sparades telefonanmälningar och mejl tidigare var för sig".

**F4. "repair reports" rendered as "felanmälningar"** (minor, PLAUSIBLE)
- Draft: C18 "31 felanmälningar fördes in"; also the title (F1) and C6 (F3).
- Source: "31 repair reports were entered".
- Case: in Swedish property management, *felanmälan* ordinarily means a fault reported by a tenant. Suppose some of the 31 entries were repair reports raised by maintenance staff themselves, for example on a round. They are repair reports but not *felanmälningar* in that sense. The material does not say who created the reports. "kept telephone reporting open for residents" does not exclude staff-originated reports.
- Smallest repair: "31 reparationsanmälningar" or "31 anmälningar om reparationer". In the title, use the neutral "anmälningarna", as Lind's quotations already do. C14 ("felanmäla per telefon" for residents) is unaffected.

**F5. "six staff" rendered as "sex anställda"** (minor, PLAUSIBLE)
- Draft: "utbildade sex anställda vid två tillfällen"
- Source: "trained six staff during two sessions."
- Case: one of the six trained people was agency or contracted staff working a shift in the maintenance team. That person is staff but not an *anställd* of Elm Quay. Nothing in the material excludes it.
- Smallest repair: "utbildade sex personer i personalen vid två tillfällen".

### Translation findings
